summary: Democratic senator from Georgia since January 2021, when his runoff victory over David Perdue, alongside Raphael Warnock's, gave Democrats control of the Senate; at 33 he was the youngest senator and Georgia's first Jewish senator. A former aide to Rep. Hank Johnson and investigative-film executive, he chaired the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations and is seeking reelection in 2026 against Rep. Mike Collins, with $33 million raised in the third quarter alone and an eight-point lead in the AJC's October poll.

chapters.title: Atlanta, John Lewis and investigative film
chapters.dek: A congressional intern at 16 and a documentary-company CEO at 26.
chapters.body:
Ossoff was born in Atlanta on February 16, 1987, and grew up in Northlake. At the Paideia School he interned for Rep. John Lewis, whom he calls his mentor [[wikipedia, ossoff-senate-bio]]. After graduating from Georgetown's School of Foreign Service in 2009 he worked from 2007 to 2012 as a national-security staffer and legislative assistant to Rep. Hank Johnson [[wikipedia]].

He then earned a master's at the London School of Economics and in 2013 became managing director and CEO of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based company producing investigative films on war crimes, corruption and trafficking, a post he held until entering the Senate [[wikipedia, ossoff-senate-bio]].

chapters.title: The 2017 special election
chapters.dek: A national test of the early Trump era, and a narrow loss.
chapters.body: In January 2017 Ossoff entered the special election for Georgia's 6th congressional district. He led the April 18 all-party primary with about 48 percent, short of a majority, and lost the June 20 runoff to Republican Karen Handel, 51.8 to 48.2 percent. It was then the most expensive House race in U.S. history [[wikipedia]]. He chose not to run for the seat again in 2018 [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: The runoffs that flipped the Senate
chapters.body:
Ossoff won the June 2020 Democratic Senate primary outright with about 53 percent [[wikipedia]]. In November he trailed Sen. David Perdue 49.7 to 48.0 percent, short of the majority Georgia requires, forcing a runoff. On January 5, 2021, he won 50.6 to 49.4 percent; with Raphael Warnock's victory in the state's other race, Democrats took control of a 50–50 Senate [[wikipedia]].

He was sworn in on January 20, 2021, at 33 the youngest senator and Georgia's first Jewish senator, on a volume of Hebrew scripture that had belonged to Rabbi Jacob Rothschild, whose Atlanta synagogue was bombed in 1958 because of his civil-rights advocacy [[toi-oath-2021, wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Investigations and votes
chapters.dek: Prison deaths, a stock-trading ban and votes on arms for Israel.
chapters.body:
As chairman of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Ossoff led bipartisan inquiries into federal prisons, abuse of women in custody and conditions in privatized military housing [[ossoff-senate-bio, wikipedia]]. A September 2022 staff report produced with ranking member Ron Johnson found that the Justice Department had failed to count nearly a thousand deaths in custody in fiscal 2021 alone; Ossoff called it "a moral disgrace" [[eji-deaths-2022, psi-deaths-2022]]. In January 2022 he introduced legislation to bar members of Congress and their spouses from trading individual stocks [[wikipedia]].

On Israel, he voted in November 2024 for Bernie Sanders's resolutions to block some arms sales, against a second set in April 2025, and in July 2025 to block a sale of 20,000 automatic rifles [[wikipedia]]. In March 2026 he voted for a War Powers Resolution limiting military action against Iran [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: The 2026 reelection race
chapters.dek: Against a Trump-endorsed congressman, with a large fundraising lead.
chapters.body:
Republicans chose Rep. Mike Collins as Ossoff's opponent in a June 16, 2026, runoff, two days after Trump endorsed Collins over Derek Dooley [[ap-runoff-2026]]. Ossoff, who has called Trump a "national embarrassment," said in April he had no interest in running for president in 2028 [[ap-runoff-2026, wikipedia]]. J Street included Collins among five AIPAC-backed Republicans in its $3 million September ad campaign [[jta-antiaipac-2026]].

The money gap is wide. Ossoff reported raising $33 million from July through September 2026 from about 760,000 donations, with $26 million on hand, after holding $42 million at the end of June; Collins raised $2.7 million in the quarter and had about $1.1 million on hand [[recorder-q3-2026]]. An AJC poll of likely voters taken October 7–15 showed Ossoff ahead 48 to 40 percent [[fox5-poll-2026]]. The election is November 3, with a runoff if no candidate wins a majority.
